$comment: Vidyra Piper voice catalog. The backend discovers .onnx files at runtime in VIDYRA_VOICE_DIR (default models/piper), so anything downloaded there appears in the picker without editing this file. This is reference documentation plus the measured cost of each tier.

$tiers.medium: Fast. Measured RTF ~0.76 on the 4-core CPU host (0.76s of compute per second of audio), ~63MB each. Default, because /create speed matters and the chunking/prosody fixes apply to it at no extra cost.
$tiers.high: Natural but ~5x slower. Measured RTF ~3.7-3.9, so about four minutes of CPU per minute of narration on this host. Worth it for a finished video you keep, not for iterating. Piper renders it at 22050Hz and the pipeline resamples to 48kHz either way.

$notes: There is no en_US-hfc_female-high. For a female voice use en_US-ljspeech-high, or keep en_US-hfc_female-medium.

en_US-libritts-high is a 904-speaker model, not a single voice. Piper defaults to speaker 0, so it works but offers no variety unless speaker selection is added; it is also the largest and slowest here.
All en_US Piper voices are 22050Hz mono natively.

voices.note: Same reader as the medium model, higher-fidelity training.
Female high-tier option; there is no hfc_female-high.
904-speaker model. Piper uses speaker 0 unless a speaker id is passed, so this adds no variety yet and is the slowest and largest option.
